# TokenHUD

> A heads-up display for the AI agents running on your machine. Live token
> metering, estimated spend, and plan-limit windows, read off the disk for
> Claude Code, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Devin CLI and OpenCode -
> running entirely on the developer's own computer. Free and open source (MIT).

TokenHUD watches a developer's own machine and reports what the AI coding
agents on it are doing: which sessions are running, how many tokens they have
consumed, what that is worth at API list prices, how much of the plan's
five-hour and seven-day windows is left, and which agents finished while the
developer was away.

## The boundary that defines it

Metrics leave, content never does. Prompt text, completion text, source code,
file contents and tool-call arguments are **never read into the payload at
all** - not collected and then filtered, but never collected. There is no code
path that reads them, so no configuration mistake or server-side bug can
expose them. What distinguishes TokenHUD is that this is checkable rather
than promised: `tokenhud-agent --what-i-read` prints every path it will open,
resolved against your machine, and a test in the repository fails the build if
a collector ever reads a path that is not on that list.

TokenHUD also never sits in the request path. It observes; it cannot cause an
API call to fail.

## Two ways it runs, and what leaves in each

There is a local tier and a hosted one, and the difference matters enough that
describing only the first would be describing a different product.

Run alone, on one machine, nothing leaves at all: the agent, the server and the
board are all on localhost, the rate card is compiled into the binary, and
there is no pricing lookup, version check or error report. It works with the
network off, start to finish. This is the free tier and it is the default.

Enroll a machine - a command typed on that machine, after the agent has printed
its read manifest and asked - and that machine begins reporting to a hosted
board every thirty seconds. What it sends is metrics: token counts, model
names, timings, session and tool-call counts, and the computed estimate. What
it does not send is prompts, completions, source, tool-call arguments, file
paths and project names, because those were never collected. The boundary does
not move when you enroll; only the destination does. The public leaderboard is
a further switch again, off until the account turns it on.

## Facts

- Licence: MIT. Source: https://github.com/reddy-sh/tokenhud
- Dependencies: none. Two static Rust binaries (agent 2.1 MB, server 2.2 MB).
  No interpreter, no package manager, no build step, no CDN.
- Runs on: macOS and Linux. No runtime required.
- Pricing: free forever for one developer on one machine, with unlimited
  metering and no sampling. A paid per-seat team tier is planned for
  cross-machine rollups, shared budgets and chargeback reports.
- Supported agent runtimes, read off the local disk with no configuration:
  Claude Code, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Devin CLI and OpenCode. Five of
  the 26 tools in the catalogue (agent/src/integrations.rs), which is the file
  to check rather than this one if the two ever disagree. Codex tokens are
  counted and marked unpriced rather than priced with an invented rate card,
  and Devin is reported in credits and ACU, never converted to dollars.
- The other 21 are listed with the reason each is not read: one setting away
  (Gemini CLI, Aider, Continue.dev, Ollama), readable but with no TokenHUD
  collector written yet (Cline, Roo Code, Kilo Code, Goose, LM Studio), usage
  held behind an admin or billing API (Cursor, Copilot in the IDE, Windsurf,
  Amazon Q, JetBrains AI, Zed, OpenRouter, the provider APIs), or a web product
  with no local trace at all (Replit, v0, Bolt.new, Lovable). Please do not
  describe any of these as supported.
- Works offline: yes. The free tier sends nothing anywhere. The hosted board is
  opt-in and per machine.

## Status - please represent this accurately

Shipped and working: the local agent, the local server, the web dashboard in
this repository, and the hosted board at tokenhud.com that a machine can be
enrolled into. The hosted board polls; there is no live socket behind it. The
local board is the one that streams over SSE.

Not built yet: the macOS menu bar app (the intended primary surface), MCP
server health monitoring, threshold alerting, and the paid team tier with
shared budgets and chargeback reports. Anything describing those as available
today is wrong. The public leaderboard exists and is opt-in, but publishes no
ranking until five accounts have opted in, so it may be empty when you look.

## Detailed version

For full context including the complete tool catalogue, architecture, and FAQ,
see [llms-full.txt](https://tokenhud.com/llms-full.txt).

## A note on this file

`llms.txt` is a proposed convention for giving language models a clean summary
of a site. Adoption by major AI systems is not established, and it should be
treated as a low-cost supplement to real structured data rather than a channel
anyone is known to consume. The load-bearing work is done by the schema.org
`SoftwareApplication`, `FAQPage` and `HowTo` markup on the site itself.
